paired.scope: Windows x64 local; one sequential sample per binary per fresh deterministic fixture
limitations: Baseline ran before candidate; host and filesystem cache conditions can differ. The especially large 0-case acquisition difference is not evidence of catalog optimization speedup.

Native lock_wait includes prerequisite checks and acquisition. Every observed acquisition has attempts=1 and outcome acquired; no queued_wait spans were emitted. No OS lock contention-only delay is established.
Catalog, registry.observe, lock and enclosing command spans overlap. They are reported separately without adding them or interpreting wall differences as isolated CPU effects.
Background producer references are nonempty and their exact bytes are preserved; preexisting native run/decision history is empty, so native history preservation assertion has empty input.
Synthetic valid schema1 records and task-owned paths approximate producer catalog cost; no production-root throughput or cross-platform acceptance follows.
Fixture payload/control state/logs remain under outer run:ff1:catalog4 ownership for root cleanup; selected target deletion does not mean full fixture cleanup.

root_assessment.reason: Exact metadata result reused within each fresh path check; immutable indexed projections preserve canonical byte order and fences, mandatory247pass and all18native performance children exit0. Measured catalog improvements without reducing full-byte observation count.
limits: One sequential pair on shared Windows host; substantial acquisition/check overhead variation.
Lock acquisition spans are not contention-only waiting; all attempts1 and noqueuedwait.
Native state history empty in synthetic fixture; nonempty producer historical references preserved.
Escaped JSON prefix normalization comparison corrected after native measurements; native cases not rerun.
No full-app or embedded runtime rebuild.
